chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahboub, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Abbas ibn Aamir, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad Al-Musli, from Abu Muhammad, from Imran, from Saeed ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a dispute occurs between two men, two angels descend and say to the foolish one of the two: 'You spoke, and you spoke, and you are deserving of what you said; you will be recompensed for what you said.' And they say to the forbearing one of the two: 'You were patient and forbearing; Allah will forgive you if you complete that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But if the forbearing one replies to him, the two angels ascend.'
ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually when two people argue and one remains patient?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the metaphysical reward for *hilm* (forbearance) during conflict, a core virtue in Shia ethics emphasizing self-restraint as a means of divine favor. The descending angels symbolize immediate spiritual validation, while the condition that the angels ascend if the forbearing party replies underscores the fragility and preciousness of maintaining silence in the face of provocation. This narrative reinforces the scholarly view that true victory lies in enduring the dispute with grace rather than engaging in reciprocal argumentation.
